round2.evidence: Step 0 persisted-enable=no grep (L138, 'empty output is the pass') has no --exclude-dir=.claude/.agents. Run on the RediStack scratch copy with the rule set installed it printed './.claude/rules/swift-quality/checks/weaken-check.sh:25:# SWIFT_BACKTRACE=enable=no printed all four.' and exited 0, so the pass can never be empty on an installed tree. The index backtrace-grep carries the excludes; the skill copy and its 're-run Step 0 on the fixed tree' instruction do not.
round2.fix: Add --exclude-dir=.claude --exclude-dir=.agents to the Step 0 grep (match the index backtrace-grep), or state in the skill that .claude lines are the installed rule set.

round2.evidence: Measured on 6.4: SWIFT_BACKTRACE=enable=false, enable=off, enable=0 and color=no,enable=no each cut the planted crash from 54 stderr lines to 13 (backtracer off), same as enable=no. Planted carriers in a scratch repo: backtrace-grep/Step 0 print only Dockerfile.1 (enable=no), ci.yml and 'enable=no,color=no'; they miss enable=false/off/0, 'color=no,enable=no', app.Dockerfile (glob is Dockerfile*), justfile, mise.toml, prod.env (.env* needs a leading dot) and devcontainer.json. weaken-check prints 7 of 11 planted carriers: it misses the same four value variants and the JSON form (a quote sits between the name and ':'), and it prints the '# SWIFT_BACKTRACE=enable=no' comment-only line.
round2.fix: Match 'SWIFT_BACKTRACE[^\n]*enable[=: "]*(no|false|off|0)\b' (value alternatives, any position in the comma list), allow an optional quote before [=:], and widen carriers to *Dockerfile*, *.env, .env*, justfile/Justfile, *.toml, *.json. Skip lines whose first non-space char is '#'.

round2.evidence: Index done-gate step 5 (L49) reads 'if swift package plugin --list | grep -q generate-documentation; then DOCC=1 ...'. gates.md L59 says the DOCC=1 before --list matters because the plugin is declared only under that variable. Plant: manifest adds swift-docc-plugin only when ProcessInfo environment DOCC == "1". Index form prints count 0 and takes the 'SKIP 5: no docc plugin declared' branch with exit 0; DOCC=1 swift package plugin --list lists generate-documentation. The two copies of the gate disagree and the index copy silently skips DocC on the manifest shape the rule itself describes.
round2.fix: Put DOCC=1 before 'swift package plugin --list' in the index copy so it is byte-identical to gates.md L59.

round2.evidence: sw-test-01 (and the sw-test-03 and sw-test-18 added-line forms) diff 'origin/main...HEAD': committed changes only. A new untracked Tests/FooTests.swift with 'import XCTest' and an uncommitted edit adding setenv( both print nothing, so empty output reads as pass on a working tree full of violations. The guard line only checks that origin/main resolves.
round2.fix: Use 'git add -N .' then 'git diff --merge-base "$BASE"' (as hatch-delta and pubenum do) so uncommitted and untracked files are in scope.

round2.evidence: pubenum gate form 'git add -N . && git diff --name-only -z ... --merge-base "$BASE" ... | xargs -r -0 perl pubenum.pl' has no BASE guard. With BASE=nonexistent (and on the PromiseKit copy, which has no origin) git prints 'fatal: bad revision' to stderr, xargs -r gets empty input and the pipeline exits 0 with no stdout; with a valid BASE the same plant prints 'public enum Bad lacks @nonexhaustive'. A mistyped or absent base is a silent pass. Sibling forms (testing, hatch-delta, apple) guard with rev-parse --verify.
round2.fix: Prefix the gate with 'git rev-parse --verify -q "${BASE}^{commit}" >/dev/null || { echo "BASE does not resolve" >&2; exit 66; }' and set -o pipefail.

round2.evidence: S1 changed-files line hard-codes origin/main with no resolve guard and no 'git add -N': on PromiseKit it printed 'fatal: bad revision origin/main' and exited 0, and an untracked new file with an undocumented @unchecked Sendable is not listed by plain 'git diff --name-only'.
round2.fix: Use the same guarded 'git add -N . && git diff --merge-base "$BASE"' form as hatch-delta.

round2.evidence: Pre-tag step runs plain 'git status --porcelain # any output is the finding'. round2.evidence: 'docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/src -w /src swift:6.4 swift build' runs as root with the repo as /src and no --scratch-path. Afterwards nio-ssh and PromiseKit .build held root-owned dirs (.build/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, repositories/*), later non-root cells printed 'find: ./.build/...: Permission denied', and the next host-path build failed with "precompiled file '/src/.build/.../SwiftShims.pcm' was compiled with module cache path '...' ... missing required module 'SwiftShims'" (and the reverse: Stale file ... outside the allowed root paths). U7 passes --scratch-path /tmp/u7 for exactly this reason; SW-LANG-03 and the floor-leg line do not.

round2.evidence: U8 says migrate with a Package@swift-X.swift in effect 'edits the dead Package.swift, exits 0 and enables nothing'. Dry-run on PromiseKit (Package.swift tools 4.0 shadowed by Package@swift-5.3.swift on 6.4): 'swift package migrate --target PromiseKit --to-feature ExistentialAny' applied 15 fix-its in 6 source files, then exited 1 with 'Could not update manifest ... (package manifest version 4.0.0 is too old: please update to manifest version 5.8.0 or newer)'; dump-package count was 0. The exit-1 taxonomy lists only 'no edits' and 'unable to find target'; this third form (source edits kept, dead manifest too old) is missing, and the exit-0 claim holds only when the dead manifest is >= 5.8.
round2.fix: Add the 'manifest version X is too old' exit-1 form to the U8 taxonomy and qualify the exit-0 claim by the dead manifest's tools version; keep 'git checkout -- .' as the recovery.

round2.evidence: Row says the flag 'exits 1 on any warning including an ungrouped one (6.4.0)'. On 6.4 the Swift-5-mode warning "passing non-Sendable parameter 'body' to function expecting a '@Sendable' closure" is not promoted: swiftc 6.4 -swift-version 5 -warnings-as-errors exits 0 with the warning (also with -strict-concurrency=targeted), exits 1 only with =complete or -swift-version 6. swift:6.3 turns the same line into 'error:' and exits 1. In the trees: 'swift build -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors' exits 0 on 6.4 with 4 Sendable warnings on PromiseKit (Box.swift:95,97) and on RediStack (HashCommands.swift:387, tools 6 with swiftLanguageModes [.v5]), while 6.3 would fail. Done-gate steps 2 and 3 and swift-upgrade U7 ('exit 0 on both toolchains') are false green on a Swift 5 mode package on the 6.4 leg.
round2.fix: Narrow the claim to Swift 6 mode (or packages with StrictConcurrency enabled), say 6.4 leaves minimal-checking Sendable warnings as warnings, and make the gate count warning lines (swift build ... 2>&1 | grep -c 'warning:') for mode-5 packages.

round2.evidence: On PromiseKit the first tsan-check.sh run printed nothing for 8+ minutes at 0% CPU: container ps showed 'swift-test --sanitize=thread' alive with a defunct '[CorePromise-tes]' runner, and a direct run of the same command logged 'ThreadSanitizer: CHECK failed: tsan_rtl.cpp:1086'. Two later runs completed (exit 1, real data races at LoggingTests.swift:95). The script has no timeout, buffers all output until exit, and only treats 'FATAL: ThreadSanitizer' (not 'CHECK failed') as 'did not run' (70). One hang in three runs.
round2.fix: Wrap swift test in 'timeout "${TSAN_TIMEOUT:-1200}"' mapping 124 to exit 70, and add 'ThreadSanitizer: CHECK failed' to the exit-70 patterns.

round2.evidence: K1 'grep -RPzo catch\b[^{};]*\{\s*\}' matches the word catch inside a doc comment and runs across lines to the next empty body: on PromiseKit it printed Sources/Catchable.swift 'catch` and `recover` to your object that conforms to `Thenable` ... public protocol CatchMixin: Thenable {}' (a protocol, not a catch clause).
round2.fix: Anchor on a statement start ('^[[:space:]]*(\}[[:space:]]*)?catch\b' with (?m)) and skip lines starting with //, ///, or *.
